item.title: The moment Mercedes’ glorious F1 comeback started? How about their lowest-ever ebb
item.description: “One of my worst days in racing,” proclaimed an aghast Toto Wolff . The scene is the paddock at the Bahrain International Circuit, the date is March 2023 and the occasion is the aftermath of the season-opening Formula One race. Mercedes have just finished more than 50 seconds off the pace set by winner Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, with Lewis Hamilton in fifth and George Russell in seventh. Behind three other cars, the former untouchable giants of F1 are, clearly, the fourth-quickest car on the grid . And in that moment, Wolff realises that – once again – he and his team of engineers and car designers back at their Brackley base have got it badly wrong. It’s worth revisiting the Silver Arrows at their lowest ebb as we revert back to the present day. On Sunday, Mercedes claimed the F1 constructors’ crown for the first time in five years, a week on from their first drivers’ world championship in six years. It is a ninth teams’ title for Mercedes, putting them level with Williams and placing them one behind McLaren on the all-time list. For Wolff, too, it puts him level with Frank Williams for the most titles for a team boss in F1 history. Mercedes celebrate in Sao Paulo (PA) Not bad, then, given the desperate doldrums the Austrian executive found himself in nearly four years ago. That day in Bahrain marked the start of this new era. A year earlier, amid the new ground-effect rule change off the back of that 2021 decider in Abu Dhabi , Mercedes’ zero-sidepod design caught the attention of everyone up and down the pit lane. And yet, as action began on the track, not only were they short of top-table pace, but their car was violently oscillating in a phenomenon called “porpoising” that nobody at HQ had envisaged. So much so that, after one race in Baku, Hamilton struggled to disembark the cockpit, such was the pain in his back. But Russell’s inaugural victory in F1 at Interlagos – Mercedes’ first win of the 2022 season, on a weekend where they claimed a one-two finish – presented a lifeline. Or so they thought at the time. Wolff has since acknowledged that it was that win which pushed Mercedes to continue down the zero-sidepod path. In a holistic game of stick-and-twist – with a rule phase not ending until 2026 – the three-pronged star decided to stick. It would prove to be a foolhardy decision. Despite seven grands prix triumphs between 2023-2025, Mercedes were still some way short of their competitors: first Red Bull, then McLaren. The three years since were something of a purgatory for Wolff who, to his credit, has never been one for hiding his emotions or ducking out of camera range in the garage, often to the detriment of a nearby headset. "Looking back in retrospect, you're saying, 'we needed these tough moments in order to grow as people or to grow as an organisation’ – but when you're down, that is quite difficult to feel,” he said on Sunday night, another constructors’ title in his back pocket. item.description: Every week, Michigan high school teams across the state are winning championships, breaking records, reaching milestones and putting together seasons worth celebrating. The Detroit News is recognizing those standout squads as Team of the Week. From nominations submitted by coaches, parents and fans, we’ve selected five boys teams as this week’s finalists. Any boys team, in any sport and from any region of Michigan, is eligible. Now it’s your turn to decide who deserves the honor. Voting is open from 10 a.m. Monday through 5 p.m. Thursday. Readers can vote multiple times, so rally your school community and get everyone involved. More: Subscribe to “Michigan Sidelines,” our high school sports newsletter The winner will be announced Friday morning in a special Detroit News post celebrating its accomplishments. Who deserves to be named the Detroit News Boys Team of the Week? Cast your vote below. Birmingham Seaholm boys tennis Birmingham Seaholm didn't just repeat as Division 2 boys tennis state champion. It dominated the competition, winning 35 matches at the state finals, the most of any program. Seaholm claimed five flight championships, with all eight flights advancing to at least the semifinals. Senior Kalil Wahab and freshman Hunter Helfman went unbeaten in five matches, winning every one in straight sets. That included a 7-6 (1), 6-4 victory in the No. 1 doubles final. Sophomore Charlie Griffith also came through, winning his second consecutive individual title at No. 3 singles. He battled through a three-set final, 6-2, 5-7, 6-3, and finished the season with a 20-4 record. It was another dominant performance for a program that continues to set the standard in Division 2. Holland Calvary Christian boys cross country Holland Calvary Christian didn't leave much doubt about who belonged at the top of Division 4 boys cross country. The team put all five scorers in the top 15 Saturday at Michigan International Speedway, cruising to its second consecutive state championship with 35 points. No boys team in any division scored better at the state finals. Senior Noah Schipper led the way with a fifth-place finish in 16:03.7. Senior Christian Getz wasn't far behind, taking seventh in 16:06.1. Senior Brody Van Tuinen also delivered, finishing 12th to earn his first All-State honor. With all five scorers in the top 15, Holland Calvary Christian put together one of the day's most impressive performances and defended its state championship in convincing fashion. Troy boys soccer Troy put together a season nobody else in Michigan boys soccer could match. The team finished 19-0-2, becoming the state's only unbeaten boys soccer program. It capped its historic run with a 2-1 victory over Livonia Stevenson in the Division 1 state championship Saturday at Grand Ledge High School. item.title: Jonathan Taylor trade rumors: Giants deal unlikely as Colts star says goodbye to fans
item.description: Jonathan Taylor’s time with the Colts is coming to an end, and everyone knows it. The team is entering a complete teardown and rebuild, meaning that after six-and-a-half seasons the running back effectively said goodbye to the fans on Sunday following the team’s loss to Dallas. "I appreciate them and it was a pleasure to put on display all of not only my hard work, but the team's hard work." @ADChernoff asked Jonathan Taylor what he hopes the fans will remember about him if this is Taylor's last game with the #Colts : pic.twitter.com/Z6bL4IMT0M — WISH-TV News (@WISHNews8) November 8, 2026 Taylor appeared destined to become the No. 1 rusher in franchise history, needing only a shade over 1,000 yards to pass Edgerrin James. Instead, he will be locked in second place, remembered fondly as a no-nonsense rusher who kept the Colts afloat during some of their most difficult times in the post-Andrew Luck era. A constant throughout the noise, the big question remaining is “where will he go?” and here’s the latest being reported on where Taylor could end up. New York Giants The Giants are reportedly out on the idea of making a deal for Taylor. They are turning their attention towards a need on the interior defensive line, and would rather make a move there — according to Jordan Raanan of ESPN . Taylor would have been a huge addition to a team in need of running help, but it seems the Giants are more convinced that Cam Skattebo can bounce back from injury, and with a bolstered interior DL presence they will be set for a playoff run. The Colts are poised to take whatever the best offer in on Tuesday Pro Football Talk has reported that Indianapolis are set on trading Taylor, which likely precipitated his comments on Sunday — knowing he would be going somewhere this week. Seemingly, the Colts have no preference on where he might end up, simply being willing to deal him to whoever gives them the best offer . It had previously been reported that Indianapolis was looking for a haul like Carolina received for Christian McCaffrey. That trade netted a 2nd, 3rd, 4th, and 5th round pick — though it seems increasingly unlikely the Colts will get as much as that deal. A handful of teams could make a trade for Taylor The Vikings are garnering a lot of attention when it comes to Taylor as a means to mitigate their woeful passing game San Francisco is a dark horse candidate to shore-up their offense in case Christian McCaffrey can’t remain healthy Cleveland could be a team to watch considering they are within striking distance of the AFC North’s top, and Quinshon Judkins has been inconsistent The Patriots will be another team to watch. Their lack of a reliable run game has put too much pressure on Drake Maye to carry the offense. A legitimate three-down back could make a huge impact for them

item.title: AFL Full Week Update: Tate Southisene, Briggs McKenzie continue to play well
item.description: SCOTTSDALE, AZ - SEPTEMBER 30: Briggs McKenzie #45 of the Atlanta Braves poses for a photo during the 2026 Arizona Fall League media day at Scottsdale Stadium on Wednesday, September 30, 2026 in Scottsdale, Arizona. (Photo by Norm Hall/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images Tate Southisene 5-for-13, 3 RBI, 4 BB, 4 K, 3 SB The Tate shows continued last week as the Braves prospect got on-base nine times again last week. Even crazier, he continues to walk just as much as he strikes out. Then, you add in the fact that he’s also a menace on the bases and it’s hard to temper expectations for him. Tate also played in the AFL Fall Stars game where he went 0-for-2…but also drew a walk and scored a run. Tate has now played in 16 games and is hitting .321/.471/.396, going a perfect 7-for-7 on stolen bases. He has also walked (14) more than he has struck out (12). Isaiah Drake 3-for-9, 4 K, CS Isaiah appeared in just three games last week, getting on-base in two of the three games. After missing a big chunk of the season due to injury, Isaiah has adjusted to the league and put together high quality at-bats, making good contact with pitches in the zone. The result is Isaiah hitting .327/.386/.404 in 17 games, going 5-for-6 in the stolen base department. Owen Carey 2-for-10, 2 RBI, 2 BB, 2 K Owen appeared in three games last week, going 0-for-4 in his first game and then getting on-base four times in the final two games. After struggling with some injuries this year, Owen has now played in 16 games in the AFL and is slashing .283/.415/.396. Briggs McKenzie 4IP 3H 0R 2BB 6K Briggs looked very solid in his single start last week, striking out six across four innings. He did a great job of establishing his slider as his premium offering and using it in-zone very well, and generating whiffs from it. Also appears that Briggs is really working on the two-seam fastball to go with his four-seam. The slider, a pitch he focused on this season, now consistently looks above average. It will be interesting to see if Briggs brings back the curveball, or if the Braves have shelved it completely, but one thing remains 100% true – he knows how to generate spin. Tanner Bauman 1IP 1H 0R 1BB 0K After struggling early at the start of the AFL season, Tanner Bauman has done a good job of commanding his pitches – finding himself in-zone much more consistently. While the stuff hasn’t particularly been great, his execution has helped him find zeroes more consistently. Tyler LaPorte 1IP 1H 0R 1BB 2K Tyler appeared in one game, striking out two. He continues to show a strong arsenal, unique mechanics, and good command. A former position player who transitioned to pitching only a few years ago, Tyler could be a player to watch should the improved command show next season.

item.title: The Devils Have Improved Against The Metropolitan Division, But There’s Still Room For Growth
item.description: ELMONT, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 07: Jack Hughes #86 of the New Jersey Devils scores the winning goal in overtime against the New York Islanders at UBS Arena on November 07, 2026 in Elmont, New York. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Saturday, the New Jersey Devils fought back from a 4-2 deficit in the third period to notch a 5-4 overtime victory over the New York Islanders . This was a watershed moment for this club for a couple of reasons. First of all, the Islanders specifically have become one of the Devils’ boogeymen over the last few seasons. New York won all four meetings with New Jersey a season ago, including the lowest point of the 2025-26 campaign: The 9-0 loss on Long Island on January 6. They also beat the Devils, 6-0, in game number two of this season, meaning in their last two games on the island leading up to this one, New Jersey was getting outscored a bewildering 15-0 by the Isles. The last time the Devils actually won a game against the Islanders was exactly two years ago today: November 9, 2024. Second, in addition to the Islanders specifically, the entire Metropolitan Division as a whole was a titanic roadblock for the Devils last season. New Jersey went a pathetic 7-17-2 against divisional foes in 2025-26. Those struggles were one of the biggest reasons why they failed to qualify for the postseason. It’s still early, but the good news is that the Devils have experienced better results against the Metro this year. After Saturday’s win, New Jersey is now 3-2-0 in intra-division games in 2026-27. That’s not amazing, but clearly it’s worlds better than the mark they posted last year. And looking past the results, the Devils’ process has been much, much better against Metro competition as well. As we look for reasons why this season’s hot start is different from past seasons’ hot starts, this improved play against the Metropolitan Division should take a prominent role in our collective analyses. They’ll have a chance to do so on Thursday when they host the Capitals in a big early-season matchup (with, presumably, Connor Hellebuyuck well-rested for that one! ). The two outliers there are obviously the first Islanders game, and the Rangers game. That October 3 game thankfully has been the only true disaster against the Metro so far. item.title: Luke Fox and Brooks Auger pitch in Fall Stars Weekend; the NL wins 7-4
item.description: SCOTTSDALE, AZ - NOVEMBER 08: Chase Harlan #11, Luke Fox #5 and Brooks Auger #36 of the National League Fall Stars pose for a photo in the dugout prior to the 2026 Arizona Fall League Fall Stars game between the American League Fall Stars and the National League Fall Stars at Salt River Fields at Talking Stick on Sunday, November 8, 2026 in Scottsdale, Arizona. (Photo by Jill Weisleder/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images The National League beat the American League 7-4 in the Fall Stars Game, and while there were no Dodger hitters involved, with Chase Harlan absent from the game, two of their pitchers made an appearance. Luke Fox and Brooks Auger came within one strikeout (5) of equaling the AL’s total for the game (6) as the two pitching staffs displayed contrasting levels of stuff. Overall, the National League struck out three times as many hitters as the AL, 18 to 6 to be precise. Fox was one of two NL pitchers to be hit with a blown save; on multiple occasions, they surrendered the lead in the middle innings before opening a three-run lead in the eighth. Fox allowed one hit and an unearned run, striking out the side in the fifth. Auger followed in the seventh with a clean frame in what was then a tied game, punching out a couple to work around a walk. The National League used 11 pitchers in total, and each one of them secured at least one strikeout, while only four of 11 did that for the AL. Winner of the Home Run Derby—replacing Chase Harlan in the contest—Aaron Parker of the Blue Jays didn’t put the ball in play in three at-bats in the All-Star Game, twice striking out and once drawing a bases-loaded walk. On the NL side of things, Yerlin Confidan doubled and walked in two plate appearances, enough to be selected MVP of the game. item.title: Oregon Ducks Football: Duck Tape Film Review Ohio State Buckeyes 2026
item.description: COLUMBUS, OHIO - NOVEMBER 7: Quarterback Luke Fahey #13 of the Ohio State Buckeyes is sacked by Nasir Wyatt #31 | Getty Images Author’s note: A full transcript of the video will be available by Monday evening. Here is a written account of my conclusions about the game for those who prefer to use the video only for play breakdowns. Oregon won this game because they were able to exploit Ohio State’s defense for big plays in the passing game, while the Buckeyes could not hit explosive plays to WR #4 Jeremiah Smith. Oregon’s offense was not efficient, but Ohio State was not consistent enough pressuring QB #8 Dylan Raiola who hit big plays when his receivers found holes in zone coverage. The Ducks’ defense shut down the short passing game the Buckeyes committed to with backup QB #13 Fahey in, and Ohio State’s run game was never a threat. The game definitively entered garbage time when the Ducks took a 38-14 lead early in the 4th quarter. This occurred at the end of Oregon’s 11th meaningful possession, whereas Ohio State only had 10 before they were too far behind to come back. The following players listed as “out” on the game day availability report are presumed lost for the season: QB #5 Dante Moore, DB #21 Aaron Flowers, ILB #23 Brayden Platt, and OL #56 Trent Ferguson. In addition both DL #55 Matthew Johnson and OL #74 Dave Iuli have been listed as out for several weeks in a row. For, presumably, different reasons WR #15 Messiah Hampton was also listed as out and will likely remain so indefinitely. Both starting running backs, RB #0 Jordon Davison and RB #6 Dierre Hill, exited last weeks game and didn’t return. Davison was out again this week, but Hill started and received the majority of the carries. In some good news, WR #3 Jeremiah McClellan was listed as a “Game Time Decision” after breaking his foot during warm ups before the Portland State game. I only spotted him once when he caught a short five yard pass in the second quarter. A couple well timed interior screens against Buckeye blitzes also resulted in explosive gains on touchdown drives. item.title: Wingin’ It for ‘MNF’ with a Buffalo take on this classic Minnesota treat
item.description: How the heck long have I been doing this anyway? It doesn’t matter; the mad-kitchen scientist is back for another season of recipes to make your Buffalo Bills game days even more memorable. For those of you new to this, it’s pretty simple. We love the Bills. We love food. Every week, you’ll get a themed recipe based on the Bills and their opponent. What could be sweeter than your favorite team on Monday Night Football ? This Minnesota-inspired cereal treat gives it a run for its money. Making this a bit more “Buffalo” was pretty easy, too. Scotcheerios The Vikings are a fun team for this series because they’re not a frequent opponent for the Bills, which means there’s still plenty to explore. When diving into Minnesota culture I came across scotcheroos, which is a type of cereal treat bar where the binding ingredient starts with corn syrup rather than marshmallow. The base recipe uses crispy rice cereal and straight corn syrup for the liquid sugar. I swap out the rice cereal and use the more “Buffalo” cereal of Honey Nut Cheerios, and then augment that flavor profile with a partial substitution on the corn syrup. Aside from that, this recipe is basically the same as this one from the Karo Syrup website , and I like to give credit where it’s due when my recipe doesn’t deviate all that much from someone else’s work. Scotcheerios Makes: About 20 treats Active time: 20 min Total time: 30 min Ingredients 1 cup semi-sweet chocolate chips 1 cup butterscotch chips 3/4 cup light corn syrup (yes I used Karo and yes they should cut me an endorsement check) 1/4 cup honey 1 cup granulated sugar 1 cup creamy peanut butter 6 cups Honey Nut Cheerios (they also should cut me an endorsement check) Essentials: Greased 9×13 pan (use glass and thank me later), medium sauce pan, large glass bowl, high-sided sauté pan, large mixing bowl, measuring cups, rubber spatulas Partially fill the high-sided sauté pan with water; place the glass bowl in the pan (see below, and be careful of splashing). Add chocolate and butterscotch chips to the bowl; turn heat to MED (about 4 of 10 on my stove); continue with step 3 while allowing chips to melt. Add corn syrup, honey, and sugar to sauce pan on MED/HIGH (about 7 of 10 on my stove). Continuously stir syrup-sugar mixture until it begins to bubble; reduce heat to MED (4 of 10) and stir for another 2 min. Remove from heat and stir in peanut butter. Add cereal to large mixing bowl; quickly fold in syrup-peanut butter mixture. Carefully pour into greased pan and press to get even bars. Stir chocolate-butterscotch chips until smooth, then quickly spread on top of cereal mixture in pan. item.description: (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 9 was brutal for the Las Vegas Raiders. Not only did they suffer a blowout loss to the San Francisco 49ers, but the Raiders also pretty much fell out of contention for the AFC West Championship. He’s a veteran of the AL East who has (mostly) crushed the Orioles’ division rivals. And he’d stabilize a position at which the Orioles were the worst in the league in 2026. item.description: Sep 15, 2026; New York City, New York, USA; New York Mets right fielder Carson Benge (3) rounds the bases after hitting a home run during the third inning against the Baltimore Orioles at Citi Field. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The 2026 Rookie of the Year Award is one of the more fascinating award races this year (at least it is in the National League, since Kevin McGonigle should run away with the American League variant). New York Mets outfielder Carson Benge is one of the three finalists, alongside St. Louis Cardinals shortstop JJ Wetherholt, and Cincinnati Reds corner infielder (though mostly first baseman) Sal Stewart. Each of the three players have an interesting and varied case to bring home the hardware in what ended up being a hotly contested race (one of which that saw a few players snubbed as finalists, namely Mets starter Nolan McLean and Colorado Rockies first baseman TJ Rumfield, both of which would place easily in my personal top three). JJ Wetherholt represents the season-long interpretation of the award. He looked like the runaway favorite to win it for months, as his exceptional defense at second base (+25 DRS) and league-average offense (101 wRC+) gave him a huge head start, especially when Carson Benge was hitting like a pitcher for about a month or so. Wetherholt, despite only playing 139 games, led all National League rookies in fWAR with 4.6 — and trailed only Kevin McGonigle in fWAR among all rookies. He was a steady player for the Cardinals from the word go. He did miss a few weeks with wrist tendonitis, but he represents the safer vote. Sal Stewart represents a vote with an older school flair. Stewart was a mediocre defender (-2 DRS at first), and his wRC+ sat at 112, so it is fair to wonder how he ended up a finalist, especially when he finished with a rather tepid 2.0 fWAR, good for fifth among NL rookies, and 17th among all rookies. How he got here was his counting stats. Stewart hit 32 home runs, easily leading all NL rookies, and finishing only behind Munetaka Murakami and Kazuma Okamodo. His 112 RBI are twenty more than any other rookie, and were third in all of baseball. Those counting stats pop off the page, and his .263/.330/.457 slash line makes it look even better. Twenty or so years ago, Stewart wins this in a landslide and no one is batting an eye. Carson Benge represents a little from Column A and a little from Column B. His 4.3 fWAR is second among NL rookies and third among all rookies, pairing a solidly above average bat (118 wRC+) with solid defense (+1 DRS). He went 20/20 on the season, hitting exactly 20 home runs and swiping 22 bags. He also has the benefit of a narrative behind him. Benge was, for lack of a better term, horrific to start his rookie season, finishing April with a 48 wRC+. He turned it on from there, finishing May with a 128 wRC+. (Photo by Stew Milne/Getty Images) | Getty Images The difference a bye week makes. It seems like the bye week set LSU back. The progress the team was making leading up to the Auburn game was all thrown away in one game against Alabama. This was the first game in which LSU faced a ranked opponent, got handled, and suffered a lopsided defeat. Here are the good, the bad, and the ugly from the Alabama game. The Good: In contrast to what some of the LSU fan base may believe, the LSU defense was actually good in this game as an entire unit. Alabama came into this game averaging 342 yards per game on the road. On Saturday, LSU held the Tide to just 285 total yards. Alabama normally averages 129 rushing yards and 213 passing yards on the road, and LSU held the Tide below both averages, allowing only 206 yards through the air and 79 yards on the ground. LSU was also able to record two sacks on Keelon Russell. But even better than the defense was Jackson Harris, who continued to showcase exactly why he is one of the best receivers in the SEC. Harris finished the game with 166 receiving yards on 11 receptions. He was the most consistent threat LSU had offensively, along with Trey’Dez Green. Green finished with 10 catches for 85 yards on 11 targets. I would like to see both players get more opportunities in the red zone to potentially help address those issues. The Bad: The red zone and offensive line continue to show up as glaring weaknesses for this team. LSU had a clear objective to beat Alabama: run the football and convert in the red zone. LSU finished the game with just 77 rushing yards, and Dilin Jones accounted for 57 of them, with 48 coming after first contact. The offensive line wasn’t getting any push and, for the first time in several weeks, gave up multiple sacks. Leavitt did run himself into a couple of them, but there were also missed blocking assignments, unblocked pressures, and pass rushers who disrupted the timing of routes in key situations. The play at the line of scrimmage also impacts how the offense can perform in the red zone. If a team gets inside the 20-yard line and cannot run the ball consistently, it allows the defense to dictate how it wants to play because there isn’t much field left to defend. The defense can treat the offense as one-dimensional, become more aggressive, and disguise blitz packages and coverages. These issues seemed like they were getting corrected, and with the return of Trey’Dez Green last week, it appeared LSU was turning the corner and progressing in the right direction offensively at the right time. item.title: Idaho to the Playoffs? There’s a Chance
item.description: SALT LAKE CITY, UTAH - SEPTEMBER 3: Joshua Wood #3 of the Idaho Vandals instructs team before the game against the Utah Utes at Rice-Eccles Stadium on September 3, 2026 in Salt Lake City, Utah. (Photo by Bryan Byerly/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images On Saturday evening Idaho smashed Eastern Washington 62-31 picking up not only their fifth win of the season but their fifth win in six games, extending one of the hottest streaks in the FCS. Once left for dead at 0-4, the Vandals are suddenly 5-5 with two weeks to play and they’ve built quite a resume along the way. Could Thomas Ford’s team actually come all the way back and nab a playoff spot if they end up running the table? It would be hard to argue against them. One could hardly fault Idaho for some of the losses it suffered in the non-conference portion of its 2026 slate. The Vandals fell to FBS Utah (who is currently 9-0 and ranked #2 in the AP Polls), a Lamar team that’s headed to the playoffs and just pulled off one of the upsets of the weekend over Stephen F. Austin, and an Abilene Christian squad that has been to the postseason two years in a row. Save for an rough last-second defeat at the hands of Cal Poly back in Week 0, the losses during the first month of the year were not ones that were necessarily catastrophic. The wins, meanwhile, are about as good as anyone in the Big Sky has right now. The Vandals got themselves on the map with their miraculous last-second win over defending national champion and then-#1 Montana State on national TV to kick off October. It was a herculean effort that kicked off the run that they’re on right now. Two weeks after that big win, they rolled into Missoula and slayed the other Montana giant with a 42-35 triumph over the Griz. They haven’t lost since. It sets up two massive games against UC Davis and rival Idaho State over the next two weeks; a pair of games that Idaho absolutely needs to win if it wants to be in consideration for one of those last few playoff spots. How realistic is it, though, that the committee would actually grant them one if that scenario were to come to pass? In that case, the Vandals would be 7-5 and 7-2 in conference play. It is not unheard of for a five-loss team to qualify for the playoffs as an at-large. In 2021 Northern Iowa got the nod at 6-5 and that was with closing their season with two losses in their final three games. Morgan State got in with a similar record in 2014 as did Indiana State that same year. There is a path for Idaho to do the same. If they were to get it done, too, the Vandals would be a team that no one would want to see in the postseason. They would be riding in with six consecutive wins on the backs of an deadly offense. Led by dynamic signal caller Joshua Wood, Idaho has gotten the better of some of the best defenses the Big Sky has to offer this year. The unit is putting up 437.6 yards and 33.9 points per game. item.title: Shenendehowa girls' and Shaker boys' soccer teams lead Section 2's massive state semifinal contingent
item.description: Shenendehowa junior Lily Iacovetti, left, and junior Lillyann Palmer celebrate a goal during the state quarterfinals against Cicero-North Syracuse on Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026, at Niskayuna High School in Niskayuna, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) With three goals already in her pocket and 25 minutes left in Saturday's Class AAA regional final, Shenendehowa forward Lillyann Palmer was given a new job. Stop the other team from scoring. Coach Holli Mulholland moved Palmer from winger to outside back to protect a lead rather than build one and the Mustangs held on to beat Cicero-North Syracuse 5-1 in steady, driving rain at Niskayuna High School. The win earned Shenendehowa its first NYSPHSAA final four trip since 2023 and put the Mustangs two wins away from their first state title since 2004. Cicero-North Syracuse spent the early portion of the game trying to contain junior Brittany Tetlack, Shen's top scorer. That left room for Palmer, a junior in her first year with the program after transferring from Colonie, who scored twice midway through the first half. "We say this every week," Mulholland said. "When you shut one down, the other one comes alive." The Northstars cut Shenendehowa's lead to 2-1 late in the first half, but senior Annika Aley restored the two-goal cushion before the break. Palmer's third goal came in the second half, and Tetlack added the final goal in the closing minutes. Palmer was quick to credit her teammates. "It takes the whole team," she said, "especially the bench and the energy that we have." For the returners, the win carried a year's weight. Shen's season ended last fall in overtime against Saratoga Springs in the Section 2 final. "These guys recognized the opportunity and punched their ticket today," Mulholland said. "These guys are tight. They're connected. They're having a good time doing what we do." Ten Section 2 teams are headed to the state semifinals: four girls' teams (Shenendehowa, Bethlehem, Schuylerville and Stillwater) and six boys' teams (Shaker, Bethlehem, Averill Park, Schuylerville, Greenville and Northville). Stillwater keeps its repeat bid alive Defending girls' Class C champion Stillwater beat North Salem 4-0, with Kamryn VanPelt scoring two goals and Brooke Hodgson adding a goal and an assist. It's Stillwater's third straight trip to the final four. Section 2 sweeps boys' regionals Section 2 will have a boys' team in the semifinals in all six classes, and five of them got there by a single goal. Class AAA: Sami Terra scored in the first half, and goalkeeper Alex Cross made a save in the final seconds to preserve Shaker's 1-0 win over Cicero-North Syracuse. Class AA: Bethlehem beat No. 1 Watertown 2-0, behind two goals from Ayaz Sajid. Those were Watertown's only goals allowed all postseason. Class A: Averill Park held off Peru 2-1 on goals from Evan LaPier and Gabriel Mussett. Class B: Colden Harrison's goal with 12 minutes left gave the Schuylerville boys a 1-0 win over Saranac.

item.title: OFFICIAL: Raúl becomes Oviedo’s coach
item.description: Real Madrid legend Raúl González has signed for Oviedo and will be their coach until the summer of 2028, the club announced on their website. Per Realoviedo.es Real Oviedo has reached an agreement to appoint Raúl González Blanco as the new head coach of its first team until June 2028. Mr. González Blanco, 49, was born on June 27, 1977, in Madrid. The new Oviedo coach spent the majority of his playing career with Real Madrid, where he became a legend after more than 15 years in the club’s white jersey. After stints with Schalke 04, Al-Sadd Sports Club and the New York Cosmos, Mr. González Blanco retired as a player in 2015. As a coach, the Madrid native began his career in Real Madrid’s youth system, joining in 2018 to coach the Cadete B and Juvenil B teams. Subsequently, in 2020, he coached the Juvenil A team, winning the UEFA Youth League. Following this success, he led Real Madrid Castilla for six seasons. Now, Mr. González Blanco takes the helm of Real Oviedo’s first team and will manage his inaugural match as the new “azul” coach this Saturday against Girona FC at the Carlos Tartiere stadium. The new Real Oviedo coach will not issue statements until his official presentation. This will be Raúl’s first chance to coach a team in professional football, given that Castilla has always been considered a team for Real Madrid’s prospects to develop.

item.title: Xavi believes Barcelona fans undervalue Frenkie de Jong
item.description: Xavi believes Barcelona fans undervalue Frenkie de Jong It is fair to say that Xavi knows a thing or two about playing in midfield for Barcelona . The World Cup winner has since hung up his boots and taken charge of the Netherlands , and as a result, has taken a Barcelona midfielder under his wings. Speaking to the Spanish media ahead of the upcoming international break, Xavi has been casting his opinion on Barcelona’s Frenkie de Jong. Xavi believes that the Barcelona fanbase should do more to appreciate what de Jong brings to the side. The former Champions League winner said ‘I think he is undervalued, but not by the coaches and his teammates. You have to listen to the people who are with him every day, because if you ask who the best midfielder is, they say Frenkie ‘. De Jong left Ajax to join Barcelona back in 2019. Now at the age of 29, de Jong has amassed over 300 appearances for Barcelona, with 20 goals scored in that time. He has won La Liga on three occasions and two Copa del Reys. Despite this success, Xavi believes that Barcelona fans expect more from de Jong, even though he has, in Xavi’s mind, been one of the best players at Barcelona. The current Dutch national team coach said ‘ De Jong is sometimes frustrated because he feels that Barcelona fans do not give him the recognition he deserves. They criticize him because he has not become the leader they dreamed of when he arrived from Ajax ‘. De Jong had to fill in at right-back for Barcelona against Atletico Madrid this weekend, something he is unlikely to do with the Dutch national team over the next week. Xavi and co face tough fixtures against Greece and Germany over the next few days. GBeNeFN | Ben Jackson

Baker Mayfield struggled, but the Buccaneers also failed to capitalize on several opportunities because of mistakes from their receiving corps. Tampa Bay forced five turnovers but still couldn’t secure the victory. The offense struggled to sustain drives despite receiving numerous chances from its defense. Buccaneers insider Rick Stroud questioned the quality of Tampa Bay’s wide receivers following the disappointing result. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Time to talk about the quality of the Bucs WRs,” Stroud wrote. He highlighted Ted Hurst’s limited involvement after the rookie dropped his only target. He caught three of five targets for 38 yards after returning from a foot injury. Meanwhile, Tez Johnson finished with 76 receiving yards on two catches. However, a 57-yard reception accounted for most of his production . Stroud also suggested Johnson dropped two catchable passes, further illustrating the offense’s problems with execution. Mayfield wasn’t blameless either. His two interceptions included a costly pick-six that helped Chicago maintain its advantage. Still, the receiving struggles raise broader questions about Tampa Bay’s offensive consistency. The Buccaneers previously entered the season evaluating their receiving depth following major roster changes. The offense needs more reliable contributions from its pass catchers, especially during critical downs. Tampa Bay now enters its bye week with several issues to address. Improving receiver execution could prove just as important as correcting Mayfield’s mistake. item.title: ‘I’m happy with where we are’: Dana White talks about Zuffa’s performance in 2026
item.description: Dana White appeared for a post-fight presser over the weekend and fielded media questions, many of which were about Zuffa’s position in the sport. White would assert that he’s very comfortable with the job his company has been doing thus far, and that he’s looking forward to growing even bigger and better in the future. Here are some excerpts of what he had to say below. White on how he’d describe Zuffa’s first year in the boxing business “We have 25 deals in 95 countries right now. One of the big things I always tell fighters is obviously making money and all these things are important when you’re a professional athlete, but how many people see the great things that you accomplish in your career, too… “I’m happy with where we are in just under a year. Really happy. We’re ahead of where I thought we might be.” On whether Zuffa has changed their position on working with sanctioning bodies “We’re sort of dealing with that on a case by case basis and if we can work it out, we’d like to for the fighters. If we can’t, then we won’t.” On whether he can get along with Eddie Hearn to promote Fury vs AJ “Yeah, I don’t have a problem with Eddie Hearn. When’s the last time you guys have heard me talk about Eddie Hearn? I mean, I don’t have a problem with Eddie Hearn…You’re asking me about Eddie Hearn right now.” On how he’d rate Zuffa’s year “I’m happy with our first year. And for me, I’ve actually had a good time this year. I’ve had a good time, you know, working in the sport, on the sport, with the team that I’ve built. We’ve had a good time and we’re happy with where we’re at just a few months into our first year.” On if he anticipates having more US cards in the coming year “I think more cards, period. Everywhere. I think you’ll see us just like the UFC, taking the fights everywhere, all over the world, not just the US and the UK.” On the split with Shakur Stevenson “Well, I don’t think we let Shakur go without a fight. I mean, we worked together and we were on a call one day and I said ‘maybe it’s just better if we all go our separate ways’ and everybody agreed. “It just didn’t work out. You win some, you lose some.” On how he plans to take over boxing when the biggest names in the sport are aligned with other promoters “Well, we’re like eight or nine months into this thing. We’ll see how it all plays out.” On whether he feels he needs to make it up to the British public for trying to take Fury vs AJ outside of the UK “[Long pause]…No. I think that obviously when tickets went on sale, it killed it. It did incredibly well and I think it would’ve done well at Madison Square Garden, too.” On who is deciding the undercard of Fury vs AJ “Well, we made some fights on the undercard…I’m not going to get into this stuff. I’ll see you in Cardiff, though.”

item.title: Texans Week 9 snap counts: How much did WR Tank Dell play in win over L.A. Chargers?
item.description: Just like that, the Houston Texans are back in the conversation for postseason chatter. In his return back to Los Angeles, C.J. Stroud threw for a season-high 384 yards and tied his career high in touchdown passes with five as the Texans rolled past the Los Angeles Chargers in a 44-22 victory at SoFi Stadium. Despite a slow offensive start, Houston found a rhythm in the second quarter and never looked back. Stroud, who wanted to see an uptick in consistency after Week 7's overtime loss to the New York Giants , threw an early pick on a pass that was batted at the line of scrimmage. He missed Nico Collins on a third-down conversion and overthrew Marvin Harrison Jr. in the second quarter. Outside of that, the former No. 2 overall pick looked like the quarterback that was promised back when drafted out of Ohio State in 2023. He connected with four different receivers, including twice with Kayshon Boutte for touchdown passes. Six passes went for gains of over 20-plus yards and were recorded as explosives. The Texans punted with less than two minutes in the second quarter. Kai Kroeger would only take the field one more time for the rest of the afternoon. For as good as Stroud was, the Texans' defense delivered a much-needed, jolt-worthy performance while attacking Justin Herbert. The Chargers' quarterback, who entered Sunday as the second-most-hit passer through eight weeks, took over at No. 1 as Houston's defense recorded a season-high eight sacks, including two each by Sheldon Rankins and Jadeveon Clowney. Entering the third quarter, Los Angeles tried to get something moving in the passing game, but an interception by Derek Stingley Jr. stopped a chance for a scoring drive. On the flip side, Stroud found Nico Collins, who made an impressive one-handed catch for a 13-yard touchdown grab, only extending Houston's lead by 26. But perhaps the best moment of the day came with Tank Dell's arrival back on the field. item.title: NFL Insiders Reveal What Detroit Lions Are Seeking Before Trade Deadline
item.description: The Detroit Lions are running out of time to make a move before the 2026 NFL trade deadline, and multiple national insiders believe general manager Brad Holmes is looking for help on defense. With Tuesday’s deadline rapidly approaching, Detroit has emerged as a team worth monitoring. The biggest priority appears to be cornerback, a position that has generated plenty of discussion throughout the season. But that might not be the only area Holmes is evaluating as the Lions prepare for the second half of their schedule. According to reporting from ESPN’s Dan Graziano, Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer, and The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones, the Lions have been exploring opportunities to strengthen their secondary. Linebacker is another potential area of interest following the frightening injury to Jack Campbell. And with the trade deadline set for Tuesday, November 10, at 4 p.m. ET , Holmes has a limited window to improve a roster that is now 6-2 following Sunday’s 19-9 victory over the Miami Dolphins. The question is whether Detroit will find the right opportunity to make a meaningful upgrade. Detroit Lions general manager Brad Holmes takes a selfie with fans at warmup ahead of the game between Arizona Cardinals and Detroit Lions at State Farm Stadium in Glendale, Arizona on Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Multiple NFL Insiders Point to Detroit’s Biggest Need The Lions’ search for cornerback help has become one of the more consistent storylines surrounding this year’s trade deadline. Several national reporters have identified Detroit as a team that could be active in the market for another defensive back. In his November 4 reporting, ESPN insider Dan Graziano revealed that both Detroit and the Chicago Bears have been checking on potentially available cornerbacks. That report provided another indication that Holmes is evaluating his options rather than simply standing pat with his current roster. item.title: Tennessee opens as a small favorite at Texas A&M
item.description: Aggies Quarterback Marcel Reed 10, The LSU Tigers take on the Texas A&M Aggies. September 19, 2026; Baton Rouge, LA, USA; at Tiger Stadium. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Tennessee completed the first of their final four objectives in the 2026 season on Saturday night, beating Kentucky 34-6. The Volunteers ran for 240 yards against the No. 6 Wildcats while holding them to just six points on the night. It was a statement win for Tennessee, but the challenges keep coming this weekend. Tennessee now heads to Texas A&M, tasked with taking on Kyle Field. The Volunteers dropped their last road test to South Carolina after melting down in the closing minutes. Tennessee also had a shaky showing at Arkansas a couple of weeks prior. Texas A&M may be in the midst of a disappointing season, but they haven’t stopped fighting. The Aggies took Alabama to the fourth quarter in Tuscaloosa, and nearly knocked of South Carolina last weekend in Columbia. Texas A&M now returns home to College Station for the first time in three weeks, set to greet Tennessee with a blackout. Almost eerily similar to a few weeks ago when the South Carolina line came out, Tennessee has opened as a 2.5 point favorite over Texas A&M, according to Fanduel Sportsbook . Unlike the South Carolina line, this spread held across markets through Sunday night and into Monday morning. The total sits at just 42.5 points. Texas A&M, despite the effort, is 4-5 on the year. The Aggies were a preseason top ten team, appearing to return a talented defense and a veteran quarterback in Marcel Reed. To be blunt, it hasn’t gone well for the Texas A&M offense or Reed. The Nashville native has thrown for just over 1,600 yards on the season while tossing eight interceptions. He’s added 206 yards on the ground. Tennessee’s aggressive defense and outstanding pass rush certainly will have an opportunity to get after Reed and force some more of those mistakes on Saturday. The Volunteers have been to College Station just one time, coming ten years ago. It was an overtime thriller, but Tennessee ultimately fell 45-38. Tennessee won the last meeting against the Aggies in Knoxville back in 2023. Saturday will serve as the sixth meeting all time between the two schools. Kickoff is set for 3 p.m. ET in College Station. ESPN will have the call.

item.title: NFL Mock Draft 2027: Eagles land Jeremiah Smith
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 31: Jeremiah Smith #4 of the Ohio State Buckeyes looks on against the USC Trojans at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum on October 31, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Eagles’ playoffs odds are bordering on an impossibility at this point. Barring some epic collapses from Philly’s NFC East rivals (possible) combined with the greatest turnaround you’ve ever seen from the Eagles offense (absolute fantasy), Howie Roseman should be looking ahead to the offseason. As it currently stands, the Eagles hold the fifth overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. I would be shocked if they pick any later than that at this point and their chances of getting a better pick feel pretty high right now. Here is a midseason simulation of the first three rounds using Pro Football Focus’ Mock Simulator. While a ton will change between now and late April, this is a good way for us to familiarize ourselves with some prospects to get excited about. Pick 1.05: Jeremiah Smith, Wide Receiver, Ohio State The biggest question going into the Eagles offseason is what happens with the quarterback position. Can Jalen Hurts play football again? Does he want to play football again? Does he want to play football for the Eagles? If the answer to all of these questions is (miraculously) yes, then the Eagles should double down on supplying Hurts with as many weapons as possible. Jeremiah Smith is the best wide receiver prospect since Julio Jones and AJ Green came out of college in 2011. There are no holes in his game and he would immediately be one of the best receivers in the NFL as a rookie. Now imagine him as WR1 with DeVonta Smith on the other side and Makai Lemon in the slot. That is a great way to get Hurts (or any other quarterback) cooking. Pick 2.36: Greg Johnson, IOL, Minnesota The turnover at offensive line this season has been a mess. Injury luck combined with youth at key positions has led to the offensive line being a real problem. Greg Johnson has been a stellar player for the Golden Gophers over the last few years. He has great size and strength, with the ability to thrive at guard or center. He’d be an immediate upgrade for Philly on the inside at all three positions he’d be able to play. Pick 3.97: Boubacar Traore, Edge Defender, Notre Dame One of the many frustrations this season has been the Eagles lack of edge pressure. While Nolan Smith is having a solid year, the rest of the Eagles edge guys have been really mediocre, at best. Boubacar Traore is a bit of a pass rush specialist, at 6’5” and 250 pounds. He has great length and burst. Coming off a dominant game against Miami, Traore is getting some real NFL hype now. Maybe he goes a lot higher than this, but right now this would be a steal for the talented pass rusher.

item.description: Jets' Aaron Glenn shuts down Will McDonald's trade request with six-word response originally appeared on The Sporting News . item.title: Incident-by-incident: Was it a bad weekend for VAR?
item.description: Manchester United's last-gasp equaliser against Aston Villa survived a VAR review for a potential foul [Getty Images] Whisper it quietly, but the statistics say video assistant referee decisions have been pretty good in the Premier League so far this season. The Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel, which looks at every contentious decision and votes whether it is right or wrong, reported just two VAR errors after eight rounds of matches. At the same stage last season, there had been six mistakes. Then came this weekend, during which almost every top-flight game had a controversial decision. BBC Sport looks at most of these situations - there really were too many to do them all - and assesses the likelihood that the KMI Panel will add to the list of errors. Manchester United 4-4 Aston Villa Incident 1: Penalty awarded to Manchester United for a foul by Boubacar Kamara on Matheus Cunha in the 16th minute. Verdict: The spot-kick was awarded because the Villa defender went through Cunha to win the ball. Replays clearly showed the first contact was on the Brazilian's foot. What the KMI Panel might say: This will be a correct decision. Incident 2: Possible foul by Senne Lammens on Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki before Patrick Dorgu's 96th-minute equaliser. Verdict : There are similarities to a goal Arsenal scored at Old Trafford last season, when William Saliba leant into United goalkeeper Altay Bayındır. Lammens was not looking at the ball, which increases the chances of a VAR intervention. What the KMI Panel might say: With the higher bar for an intervention in the Premier League, and minimal contact, it is unlikely to be a VAR error not to disallow the goal. Arsenal 1-0 Hull Incident: Kai Havertz was pulled down inside the area by Nobel Mendy. The VAR, Michael Oliver, sent referee Farai Hallam to the pitchside monitor for a penalty, but it was not given due to an offside offence by the Germany international. Verdict: BBC Sport covered this incident in detail on Saturday . As the foul happened before any potential offside offence, the penalty should have been awarded. What the KMI Panel might say: Even though it feels wrong to reward a player in an offside position with a penalty, the law says otherwise and this is likely to be a mistake. Leeds 1-0 Tottenham Incident: Omar Bogle fouled Mathys Tel, with referee John Brooks giving the free-kick but no sanction for the Leeds player. The VAR, Tony Harrington, opted not to send Brooks to the monitor for a red card. Verdict: BBC Sport covered the merits of this incident on Saturday . It was a difficult call for the VAR, because Bogle caused the foul with his supporting rather than his challenging foot. Still, it was a very painful challenge and some believe it should have been a red card. What the KMI Panel might say: Was it an unfortunate incident, or a tackle which endangered the opponent?
